newsitem.title: CANADA: Toronto stocks end mixed despite bank rally.
newsitem.headline: Toronto stocks end mixed despite bank rally.

* Toronto stocks closed mixed as banks rallied but conglomerates and oils weakened. * Awaiting Greenspan's testimony.
Toronto stock closed mixed in light trading on Tuesday as the weighty bank sector rallied, but conglomerate and oil groups weakened on profit-taking.
The Toronto Stock Exchange's key 300 Composite Index added 5.26 points to 6247.78, edging closer to its lifetime high of 6260.73 set on February 19.
"All the activity was centered in the bank sector... fueled by some solid earnings," said Ira Katzin, investment advisor at RBC Dominion Securities.
The financial services sector, which makes up 17.55 percent of the 300 index, jumped almost 2.1 percent.
Two of Canada's largest banks -- Bank of Montreal and Bank of Nova Scotia -- reported better than expected first-quarter earnings.
Gains were balanced by losses in conglomerates, oils and other sectors as investors reaped profits after recent gains, Katzin said.
Volume was 105.75 million shares worth C$1.67 billion. Declining issues beat advances 525 to 463, while 307 traded unchanged.
Of Toronto's 14 sub-indices, five rose led by banks, forestry products and media. Nine stumbled including conglomerates, oils, consumer products and base metals.
Market players are awaiting U.S. Federal Reserve chairman Alan Greenspan's Humphrey-Hawkins testimony on Wednesday. The second part of his testimony was rescheduled for March 5.
--- HOT STOCKS ---

* Canadian Imperial Bank of Commerce rose 1.60 to 67, leading Canada's largest banks higher. Third largest Bank ofMontreal gained 1.10 to reach 52.90 and fourth ranked Bank of Nova Scotia added 1.25 to hit 52.90.
